Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If you're in the question queue, please press star two to remove yourself. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Technologies' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Tom Blackwell, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on our current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Global Aerospace Technologies delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, commercial aviation, and space systems. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. Today, I'll highlight our key achievements, including backlog growth, R&D investments in next-generation platforms, drivers behind our strong aftermarket performance, commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery, and the geopolitical factors bolstering defense spending.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to accelerate our future growth trajectory. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including hypersonic interceptors and integrated air defense, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with ramping OEM partner production.

I'll now turn it over to Tom for a deeper dive into our financial results.

Tom Blackwell:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. Let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $5.7 billion, representing a 14% increase year-over-year, driven by higher volumes in defense programs and aftermarket services. Our diluted earnings per share were $2.25, exceeding our expectations. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $4.8 billion in cash and equivalents, providing ample liquidity for investments and shareholder returns. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at revenue of $22.5 to $23.0 billion and EPS of $8.75 to $9.00. We are actively managing our costs while investing in key growth initiatives, and we remain focused on returning capital to shareholders through our dividend program and ongoing share repurchases.

Key financial highlights include a gross margin of 23.1%, up 110 basis points year-over-year; operating income of $1.15 billion; and free cash flow of $925 million.

Before moving on, let me dive deeper into some of our strongest metrics this quarter, starting with backlog growth, which underscores the durability of our franchise positions across defense, commercial aviation, and space systems. As of September 30th, our total backlog stood at $48.7 billion, up $2.9 billion or 6.3% sequentially from $45.8 billion at the end of Q2, and up a robust $8.1 billion or 19.9% year-over-year from $40.6 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our 11th straight quarter of backlog expansion, reflecting sustained demand amid escalating geopolitical risks, commercial air traffic recovery, and our positioning in high-growth areas like hypersonics and next-gen propulsion.

Breaking it down by segment: Defense backlog grew to $32.4 billion, up $2.1 billion or 6.9% quarter-over-quarter and $6.2 billion or 23.7% year-over-year, propelled by awards in integrated air and missile defense. We secured a $1.8 billion sole-source contract from the U.S. Missile Defense Agency for LRIP Lot 7 of our next-gen hypersonic glide vehicle interceptors, building on Block 4 PAC-3 MSE successes. We're also benefiting from accelerated funding for the NGAD program, where our adaptive cycle engine is in advanced EMD phase, with $450 million in new options exercised this quarter.

Commercial aviation backlog expanded to $11.2 billion, up $650 million or 6.1% sequentially and $1.5 billion or 15.5% year-over-year. This is driven by post-pandemic ramp-ups at partners like Boeing and Airbus, with composite wing spar assemblies for the 777X reaching full-rate production and adding $420 million in firm orders. Supply chain stabilization has unlocked pulls from the A320neo family, where our geared turbofan modules are booking at a 1.3x book-to-bill.

Space and advanced systems backlog hit $5.1 billion, up $150 million or 3.0% quarter-over-quarter and $400 million or 8.5% year-over-year, including a $320 million NASA COTS follow-on for our reusable orbital transfer vehicle tied to the Artemis lunar architecture, and initial tranches from the U.S. Space Force’s VLEO satellite constellation, where our Hall-effect thrusters are qualifying for proliferated LEO operations.

Our overall book-to-bill was 1.25x for the quarter—above the 1.0x organic growth threshold—and 1.18x on a trailing 12-month basis. Funded backlog is 62% of total, or $30.2 billion, with the rest in probable options and IDIQ ceilings. This provides exceptional visibility: 28-30% converts in FY25, 55-60% by FY27.

Regionally, the U.S. is 78% of backlog, supported by the FY24 NDAA’s 7% topline increase to $886 billion and Ukraine/Israel aid. International is 22%, up from 19% YoY, with $1.2 billion in Saudi GEA program sustainment for F-15EX avionics, NATO ramps in Poland and Finland for Patriot and F-35, and AUKUS Pillar II’s $280 million in hypersonic pre-contract funding from Australia and the UK.

This surge validates our $2.4 billion FY24 capex, with 40% for digital thread like MBSE to compress NGAD and hypersonic timelines by 18-24 months. We're derisking supply chains with U.S.-based rare earth fabbing for thruster magnets and titanium sponge localization. We’re pursuing $15-20 billion near-term, positioning for 15-18% CAGR through FY28. Our teams are executing flawlessly, supporting our raised guidance.

Shifting to another key growth driver, our R&D investments in next-generation platforms and technologies. In this sector, innovation is a survival imperative amid great power competition, supply chain issues, and evolving threats from peers like China and Russia. In FY24 year-to-date, we've allocated $2.8 billion annualized pace to R&D—about 18% of revenue and up 22% from FY23's $2.3 billion. This is our third year of double-digit growth, outpacing industry averages. Roughly $1.1 billion is company-funded IR&D to de-risk tech ahead of awards, with $1.7 billion from CRAD via DoD programs like NGAD and DARPA hypersonics.

By initiative, aligned with NDAA priorities like JADC2: Advanced air dominance took 38% or $1.06 billion, accelerating digital engineering on sixth-gen fighters building on F-35 heritage. Our open mission systems for CCA swarms hit TRL 7, with 5,000 simulated flight hours reducing timelines 25% via MBSE, positioning for USAF's $20 billion NGAD awards in FY25.

Hypersonics and directed energy got 27% or $756 million, with scramjet prototypes at Mach 8 in NASA Langley tests, integrating kill chains with Raytheon solid-state lasers scaling to 300 kW against DF-17 threats. This grew 35% YoY with $450 million new contracts, eyeing AUKUS exports.

Space and resilient architectures: 20% or $560 million for responsive space, reusable orbital vehicles cutting costs 40%, and pLEO for missile warning with AI edge processing against jamming—up 28% with $300 million SDA Tranche 2.

The rest, 15% or $420 million, enables AI/ML predictive maintenance, quantum cyber, sustainable propulsion, and hybrid-electric for eVTOL to tap the $1 trillion market.

Regionally, U.S. DoD is 68% at $1.9 billion from the $886 billion FY24 budget; Europe 15% via NATO with €250 million GCAP Tempest tech transfer; Asia-Pacific 12% fastest-growing with India MRFA and South China Sea offsets, localizing 30% drone production in Hyderabad.

These yield 3x ROI over five years, 47 new patents up 19%, digital twins shaving 18 months off schedules. With $4.2 billion next-gen backlog, we're leading peers, setting the tempo against disruptors.

Next, our aftermarket business, the crown jewel delivering high-margin recurring revenue. In Q3, it grew 18% year-over-year to $2.4 billion, 42% of segment sales, with margins at 24.2%—up 210 basis points. Driven by fleet utilization, maintenance cycles, and digital transformation.

Fleet utilization is key: Commercial global ASK recovery at 85-90% pre-pandemic per IATA. Our 12,000+ engine base—CFM56 on 737s, LEAP on A320neo/737 MAX—hit 99.5% dispatch, with narrowbody hours up 22% to 1.2 billion on APAC/LatAm LCCs. APAC at 92% for AirAsia/IndiGo; North America 88% tempered by pilot shortages; Europe 86% with Ryanair LEAP orders up 25% QoQ.

Defense stronger: T700/F110 on Black Hawks/F-16s up 15% on Ukraine aid $60 billion YTD and NATO 2% GDP; Middle East F-15EX added 8%, MTBUR to 5,200 hours via EHM.

Maintenance cycles compressing: Commercial D-checks/PRSs down 10-15%, MRO backlog $1.8 billion up 28%; Lufthansa CFM56 up 35% with 45-day turns via additive hot-sections, 18% cost cut. Defense F-35 ODIN transition boosted F135 sustainment 32%.

Tech supercharges: Digital suite/AI PHM cuts removals 22%, 95% LLP accuracy for forward-pricing ESAs; 70% digitized MRO with blockchain; 3D-printing 40% F110 blades, lead times to 12 weeks; Boeing 777X hybrid MRO.

65% backlog $28 billion in 10+ year TSAs/ESAs through 2030; FY25 NDAA $850 billion adds hypersonic sustainment $200 million. Risks like Boeing 38/month ramp offset by vertical integration. Guide $9.5-9.8 billion full-year, 23.5% margins, 12-15% EPS CAGR.

On commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery: Q3 saw 155 units, up 28% YoY, on track for full-year 570-610, up 22% from 2023. Narrowbodies 122 on 737 MAX ramps post-FAA recert; widebodies 33 Horizon 787s post-titanium fixes.

Orders 210 gross, backlog $528 billion (8+ years); net 185, pricing up 5% to $142 million average. 2025 targets 750-800, narrowbody 52/month, widebody 10/month.

Trends: IATA load factors 84.5%, RASM +4.2%; narrowbody 78% backlog. Regions: APAC 42% with China ramp post-COVID, 30% 2025 growth; NA 31% ASM +6.8%; Europe/ME 27%.

Challenges: Supply shaved 15 deliveries; $1.2 billion capex for digital twins (22% variability cut), 3D titanium (40% parts), 150 robots, 98% parts availability.

Synergies: 787 composites to B-21, 737 lines to KC-46; $120 billion defense backlog subsidizes. Q4 guide 160-170; 35% narrowbody share by 2027.

Finally, geopolitical factors: SIPRI 2024 spend $2.5 trillion up 7.2%; US FY25 $849.8 billion up 4.1%, munitions +28% to $29.8 billion.

Europe: Ukraine aid $200 billion depletes stocks, our Javelin variants 50,000+ units $1.2 billion backlog; Poland +30%, Germany €100 billion for PAC-3/Eurofighter; SkyNet C4ISR +45% orders, Q3 revenues $450 million up 22% QoQ.

Middle East: 10,000+ intercepts, FMS $80 billion; Viper $750 million IDIQ UAE; Saudi $20 billion THAAD pursuits.

Indo-Pacific: $500 billion spend; Taiwan Harpoon 400+; AUKUS $3 billion hypersonics; Japan/SKorea F-35 aftermarket $300 million; $11 billion UFP munitions.

Munitions multi-year: 155mm down 60%, $5-7 billion buys; $250 million AI R&D TRL 7 by 2026; domestic alloys cut inflation. Backlog $28.5 billion up 18%, 1.4x book-to-bill; FY24 $6.8-7.0 billion revenue +15%, EPS $4.85-5.05, margins 12.8%.

These tailwinds sustain 5-7% global CAGR; we're diversified across threats.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, Tom. Operationally, we've seen significant supply chain improvements, enabling production ramps on key programs like hypersonics and commercial engines. Investments in automation and digital technologies, including MBSE and additive manufacturing, are boosting efficiency and cutting costs by 15-20% on average.

Dr. Raj Patel:
To add a tech perspective, our advancements in AI-driven PHM and digital twins are integrating seamlessly across platforms, enhancing reliability and speeding development cycles.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Josh Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth, particularly the funded portion and conversion outlook?

Alex Rivera:
Certainly, Josh. As Tom detailed, funded backlog is $30.2 billion or 62%, with 28-30% converting in FY25. This visibility, combined with 1.25x book-to-bill, positions us strongly amid demand tailwinds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the R&D investments—how are you measuring ROI and prioritizing amid budget pressures?

Tom Blackwell:
Emily, our R&D-to-revenue at 18% is high-end, projecting 3x ROI via follow-on contracts, evidenced by 47 new patents and 18-month schedule savings. We're prioritizing JADC2-aligned tech like CCA and hypersonics, with $4.2 billion backlog de-risking it.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
Regarding the aftermarket performance, what are the biggest drivers for sustained margin expansion?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Mike, fleet utilization at 85-90% commercial and higher defense, plus compressed maintenance cycles, are key, amplified by our digital suite reducing removals 22% and additive manufacturing cutting costs 18-30%. Long-term ESAs provide stability.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
